Implementation Plan

I've planned this as a one-file change: delete `changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md`, which describes a change that does not exist. Nothing else changes, following the answer to Q1 (option A).

**Planning ref.** The planning context says `main` at `a29f36d04f57c101345400ad998bca229557eafc`. The isolated workspace snapshot I read is `8d331ce` on branch `isolated`. No integration branch is declared, so there is no integration branch mismatch.

**What I checked.**
- **`changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md`** says three things:
  - the low-severity test was renamed to `test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_fail`;
  - "Since #6539 the cap converts a low or medium `keep_fixing` decision to `fail` and never records a waiver or advisory follow-up";
  - "The poller is unchanged."
- **`tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:6649`** is still `test_security_pass_cap_converts_low_keep_fixing_to_advisory`, and its comment says to keep that name. It asserts the advisory path:
  - status `complete` and `security_pass_status == "passed"`;
  - one waiver row whose justification starts with `[keep_fixing capped after 2 judge round(s); converted to advisory follow-up]`;
  - one created issue labelled `ai:security` with the title `[security-pass] Advisory: SEC-TEST-1 (low, scripts/example.py:1)`;
  - no `ai:security-pass-failed` label and no `SECURITY_PASS_FAILED` log line.
- **`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (the block starting "Convergence backstop for medium/low findings only (#6517, #6729)", around lines 7359-7392)** turns capped medium/low `keep_fixing` decisions into `accept_with_followup` and logs `SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_KEEP_FIXING_CAPPED`.
- **`changelog.d/6906-security-cap-low-medium-advisory.md`** already describes this behaviour correctly: low and medium become advisories at the cap, and high, critical and unrated findings are never waived. It also records that #6539's "convert to fail" rule was reversed.
- **Nothing else** in the repo refers to `keep_fixing_to_fail` or to the #6914 fragment.
- **`tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py`** does not require a fragment per PR, so deleting this one breaks no test.

**Conclusion.** PR #6925 left nothing true to report. The fragment's behaviour claims are false, and #6906's fragment already covers the real rule. So the decision's "delete" branch applies, not the "rewrite" branch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends changelog.d fragment workflow (scripts/assemble_changelog.py)
Scope-mode justification: The approved answer (Q1: A) limits the fix to the stale changelog fragment. The code, tests, README.md and agents.md already agree on the advisory rule (#6729, restored by #6906), and the decision forbids changing them. The fragment is only wrong text: the test was not renamed, the poller does not use a "convert to fail" rule, and #6906's fragment already describes the real behaviour. Deleting the fragment is the complete fix. A rewrite would only repeat #6906's entry in the release notes. This is the smallest change that keeps a false line out of the next release. Following §6 Core Priorities (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), it keeps the decided security policy in place and fixes the record.

## Files likely to change
1. `changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md`: delete it.

No other file changes. In particular, leave these alone:
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
- `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`
- `README.md`
- `agents.md`
- `changelog.d/6906-security-cap-low-medium-advisory.md`
- the `agents.d/` directory (add no fragment)

## Functions or modules to implement
None. This only removes a file.

## Data structures affected
None. `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` simply has one fewer fragment to fold at the next release (in `mark-stable.yml` or `test-and-mark-stable.yml`).

## API or interface changes
None. The next `CHANGELOG.md` release section will not contain the false #6914 bullet. The real rule still appears there through the #6906 fragment.

## Decisions

### D1 — Delete the stale fragment rather than rewrite it
- Chosen: Delete `changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md`.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Rewrite line 2 to say that the low-severity cap test expects an advisory follow-up. This would only repeat the #6906 entry and describe a test change that #6925 did not make, since the test name and assertions match what #6906 restored.
  - Option B, reversing the policy to fail-closed. The decision rejected this because it would undo #6729 and #6906.
  - Option C, changing nothing. Rejected because it would release a false changelog entry.
- Why: The approved plan says to delete the fragment if #6925 left no real change to report. The test still has its historical `_to_advisory` name and still asserts the advisory path. The #6906 fragment already documents the user-visible rule. Nothing true is left for #6914's fragment to say.

### D2 — Add no replacement changelog fragment for this PR
- Chosen: The PR deletes the stale fragment and adds no new `changelog.d/` entry.
- Alternatives considered: Add a `fixed` fragment saying the changelog was corrected.
- Why: The deleted fragment was never released, so released `CHANGELOG.md` and runtime behaviour are unchanged and there is nothing user-visible to report. No contract test requires a fragment per PR.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundaries:** none touched. No runtime code, workflow, prompt or credential path changes.
- **Authorization:** no new endpoints or surfaces.
- **External input:** none consumed.
- **Abuse cases:**
  - A false changelog line could lead operators to believe a project at the cap with only low/medium findings will terminalize as `ai:security-pass-failed`, when it actually completes with advisory follow-ups. Removing the line keeps the operator-facing record accurate.
  - The security policy itself does not change: high, critical and unrated findings are still never waived at the cap.
- **Money handling:** not applicable.

## Risks and edge cases
- **Conflict found (CONFLICT DETECTION).** The issue's suggested fix (make the poller fail-closed, rename the test, edit README.md and agents.md) contradicts the current code, tests and docs. The approved answer resolved this as option A, and this plan follows it.
- **A release may already have folded the fragment.** At planning time the fragment is still in `changelog.d/`, so it is unreleased. If a release folds and deletes it before this PR merges, the PR's delete becomes a modify/delete conflict, or the file is simply missing. The implementer should then leave `CHANGELOG.md` alone; correcting released history is a separate issue. `review_conflict_prepare.sh` keeps the PR's copy of a folded fragment only when the PR *changed* it, so a pure deletion would not be reintroduced.
- **The issue body says "Close each one with the smallest change".** Deleting one file is the smallest change.

## Testing considerations
- No new tests.
- The implementer can run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py tests/test_assemble_changelog.py -q`, on the pinned toolchain, to confirm the fragment directory and assembler contracts still pass. Mark the result UNVERIFIED if dependencies are not installed.
- Optional dry check: `python3 scripts/assemble_changelog.py` in its check or dry-run mode (if it has one) should report one fewer fragment and no errors.
- Check that `git diff --stat` shows only `changelog.d/6914-security-pass-cap-low-test.md` deleted.

## Pre-execution self-check
- The plan follows answer Q1: A, using the decision's "delete" branch: the test still describes the advisory path, and #6906's fragment already covers the behaviour.
- Every claim above comes from files read in this run.
- No automation paths (`scripts/`, `.github/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`) are touched, so the automation-path grant guard does not apply.
- No agents.md edit and no new log prefixes.
- PR body: link the issue with `Fixes #<this issue>`, since this is a standalone activation-fix issue and not an orchestrator tracking issue. Run `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py` on the body before submitting.
